scheme_name: CCAMP (Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms)
overview: CCAMP (Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms) is an initiative supported by the Department of Biotechnology, Government of India, established in 2009 to enable cutting-edge life science research and innovation. It serves as a catalyst for bioscience research and entrepreneurship by providing research, development, training, and services through state-of-the-art technology platforms. CCAMP promotes entrepreneurship and innovation through seed funding schemes, mentorship programs, and bio-incubation facilities, fostering an entrepreneur-friendly culture in academic and research environments.
objectives: Enable cutting-edge life science research and innovation
Facilitate bioscience research and entrepreneurship through technology platforms
Promote entrepreneurship and innovation via seed funding schemes and mentorship programs
Provide bio-incubation facilities to support early-stage startups
Bridge the gap between academic research and industry through translation and commercialization
Support startups in healthcare, agriculture, environment, and industrial biotechnology sectors
Nurture ideas and innovations into successful startups through various seed funding schemes
Widen the pipeline of startups and ensure long-term operational sustainability of incubators
eligibility: Eligibility varies across specific seed funding schemes but generally includes: Indian startups registered under Companies Act, 2013; at least 51% shareholding by Indian promoters (excluding OCI/PIO); turnover not exceeding specified limits (e.g., Rs 25 cr or Rs 100 cr depending on scheme); incorporation within 5-10 years; working on innovative, technology-driven products or services in life sciences, healthcare, agri-tech, or related sectors; product-oriented (not service-oriented); novel technology with IP generation potential; competent technical and business team; sound commercialization strategy and roadmap; clear understanding of end-user/customer and market size; sound business plan and company vision. Some schemes require residency at C-CAMP incubation (e.g., NIDHI SEED Support Scheme requires 3 months of incubation).
benefits: CCAMP provides access to state-of-the-art technology platforms, research and development support, training, mentorship, networking opportunities, and incubation facilities. Financial benefits include seed funding, grants, equity-based investment, and debt/convertible debentures through various partnered schemes (e.g., BIRAC SEED, AIM Seed, LEAP, NIDHI SEED, SISFS). Non-financial benefits encompass prototype generation, proof-of-concept studies, scaling-up support, patent analysis, market research, professional consultancy, enterprise building, IPR support, and guidance on regulatory pathways. Startups also gain access to investor networks, demo days, and follow-on funding opportunities.
financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme: BIRAC SEED offers equity-based investment up to INR 30 Lakhs; AIM Seed uses a co-investment model where CCAMP invests INR 12.5 Lakhs matched by private investors; LEAP Fund provides up to INR 1 crore per startup via equity or equity-linked instruments; NIDHI SEED Support Scheme offers INR 25 Lakhs (up to INR 100 Lakhs for exceptional cases) based on equity or equity-linked instruments; SISFS provides up to INR 20 Lakhs as grant for proof-of-concept/prototype/product trials and up to INR 50 Lakhs for market entry/commercialization/scaling via convertible debentures or debt; SIIP offers fellowship of INR 50,000/month and a kick-start grant of INR 5 Lakhs. Funds are typically disbursed in milestone-based instalments and cover activities like proof-of-concept, prototype generation, scaling, validation, market research, hiring, consultancy, IPR, operational costs, and mentoring.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant seed funding scheme (e.g., BIRAC SEED, AIM Seed, LEAP, NIDHI SEED, SISFS, SIIP) based on eligibility and focus area. 2. Ensure compliance with scheme-specific eligibility criteria (e.g., incorporation, shareholding, turnover, innovation focus). 3. Prepare required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, business plan, pitch deck, details of technology/IP, team credentials, and financials. 4. Apply via the designated application portal (commonly https://www.ccamp.res.in/funding/content/application-form-seed-funding-schemes or scheme-specific URLs like https://www.birac.nic.in/desc_new.php?id=395 for SIIP). 5. Submit the application before the deadline (if applicable). 6. Undergo screening and evaluation by a panel of experts based on scientific strength, commercialization potential, societal impact, team strength, and implementation plan. 7. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentations or interviews. 8. Await final selection and funding disbursement upon agreement to terms (e.g., equity sharing, milestone reporting).
required_documents: Details of technology, innovation, and intellectual property (IP)
Information on founders and team (educational/professional background)
Shareholding pattern showing at least 51% Indian promoters
Details of any prior government or private funding received
Proof of residency at C-CAMP (for schemes like NIDHI SEED requiring incubation)
Product prototype or proof-of-concept data (if applicable)
deadlines: Varies by scheme: NIDHI SEED Support Scheme open till 31st July 2026; LEAP Fund has rolling applications; AIM Seed has rolling applications; BIRAC SEED has rolling applications; SIIP has rolling applications; SISFS has rolling applications. Some schemes like TIDE 2.0 G2C have specific windows (e.g., 13th Nov to 20th Nov 2025). Many operate on a rolling basis with periodic review cycles.
implementing_agency: Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India
caveats: Funding is scheme-specific and not guaranteed; meeting eligibility does not assure selection
Some schemes require equity sharing or co-investment from private partners
Startups must not have received excessive prior government support (e.g., SISFS bars those with >INR 10 lakh from other Central/State schemes)
Certain schemes are restricted to specific sectors (e.g., SIIP focuses on 'Aging and Health' and 'Food and Nutrition')
Residency at C-CAMP incubation may be mandatory for some schemes (e.g., NIDHI SEED requires 3 months of incubation)
Funds must be used for approved activities only (e.g., proof-of-concept, prototyping, market entry)
Intellectual property generated may be subject to sharing or reporting obligations
Continued funding may depend on milestone achievement and progress reporting
